issues.title: Terminology: two kinds of context need separate terms
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
## Problem

"Dialog Context" is used for the context the agent builds, which ACP
does not transmit. But ACP also carries information about the dialog
beyond its identifier, such as its lifecycle state, version, creator,
negotiated modalities, and lifetime. That information has no name.

## Proposal

```
Dialog Context:
: The information that ACP carries to correlate and maintain an
  agentic dialog, such as the Agentic Dialog Identifier, the lifecycle
  state, the participant that created the dialog, the negotiated
  modalities, and the lifetime.

Task Context:
: The context an agent builds and maintains over an agentic dialog,
  such as conversation history, instructions, and intermediate
  results. ACP does not transmit or interpret it.
```

Section 4.2.9 would then read "ACP doesn't Transmit Task Context".

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I cleanly separated this now, but used "dialog context" and "LLM context".

issues.title: Two-party model in Section 5 conflicts with other sections
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
## Problem

The draft describes the dialog topology in four inconsistent ways:

- Section 5: "fundamentally two-party"; topologies are built from
  "two unrelated instances of ACP ... connected only through delegated
  identities".
- Section 6.1.1: the ADID correlates messages "at every hop", is used
  by intermediaries, and "a dialog can involve more than two
  participants".
- Section 8.4: group communication with membership that changes during
  an exchange.
- Section 11: identifiers "persist across intermediaries and trust
  boundaries", which Section 5's model rules out.

## Proposal

Support both models, and state it once in Section 5:

```
A participant can carry a dialog to the next hop, or create a new
dialog, with a new dialog context, linked to the one it received. A
new dialog is created at a trust boundary and wherever local policy
requires it. Only the participant that creates the new dialog knows
the link. A dialog can have more than two participants, such as
members of a group.
```

Then align Section 11: a dialog context identifier does not cross a
trust boundary.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I've cleaned this up so it is clear that its 2-party, but that the ADID and principal identities are propagated into downstream agentic dialogs. I added a diagram as well to clarify this.

issues.author: tireddy2

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I removed the "intermediary" concept from the doc, and instead talk about delegating agents.

issues.title: Authorized agent
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: Section 6.1.2: who is "an authorized agent" here? It is not defined.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: Removed the word "authorized". It is not needed for this sentence to be understood anyway.

issues.title: Resumption: verify the resuming party and handle interrupted operations
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
Section 6.1.2 says an authorized agent uses the ADID to re-associate
with the dialog. Holding the ADID is not enough. On resumption, the
receiver should verify that the resuming party is the one whose
exchange was interrupted, that its dialog context is current, and that
the dialog is still authorized.

Also, resuming the dialog does not show whether an interrupted
operation completed. Its outcome stays unresolved until it can be
established, and resuming alone does not justify sending it again.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
Added: Of course, proper authentication is also required - knowledge of the ADID is insufficient for the newly formed connection to be associated to the agentic dialog. 

Also added: Resumption also requires protocol agreement on whether the client needs to reply prior input, or whether the server had already processed it.

issues.title: Should dialog identifiers be resistant to forgery?
issues.author: maxpassion
issues.body:
During the BoF discussion, the concern was raised that identifiers are too easy to forge.

Is there a need for identifiers to be verifiable, so that the party receiving an identifier can tell whether it belongs to the dialog it claims to represent?

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
I don't think this is complex. a dialog identifier should be a UUID, unique in space and time, and unguessable. Knowledge of an ADID provides no information whatsoever about the agentic dialog. KNowledge of he ADID is also insufficient for a client to connect to the server, and access the agentic dialog in any way - the client must also authenticate itself, and be authorized for such access. 

I've added this to the doc.

issues.title: Distinguish a failed check from one that could not be completed
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
Section 6.1.2 lists lifecycle events but not the states they move between, so it cannot say, for example, that a terminated dialog
cannot be resumed. Lifecycle states and transitions are being discussed for draft-zahed-agentproto-refarch:
https://github.com/zaheduzzaman/overall-aiproto-architecture/pull/8

Cancellation of prior input is a task-level action, already covered in Section 6.1.6, and rehydration is a client synchronizing its local
storage. Neither changes the state of the dialog, so they do not belong in the lifecycle list.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I think the actual state machine is outside the scope of this doc and would belong in the actual protocol spec. I did clarify that terminated means it cannot be resumed.

issues.title: Add an operational flow
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
The draft describes each function separately but does not show how
they combine in one interaction, from selecting an agent to completing
the task. An operational flow covering connection, authentication,
authorization, dialog creation, delegation, continuity, and completion
is being added to draft-zahed-agentproto-refarch:
https://github.com/zaheduzzaman/overall-aiproto-architecture/pull/7

Suggest including it here.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I think this is too low level and belongs in the protocol doc.

issues.title: Resuming does not establish the outcome of an interrupted operation
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
Section 6.1.4 describes a server failing while processing a request,
but not what the client does after resuming the dialog.

For example, the client asks an agent to book a room, and the
connection drops before the reply arrives. After resuming, the client
cannot tell whether the room was booked. Sending the request again
could book a second room. The client should first find out whether
the request completed.

See Section 4.2 of draft-agentic-ai-usecases-requirements:
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-agentic-ai-usecases-requirements/

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
I added:

* Resumption: Resuming input or output, requiring (if needed) creation or modification of transport connections to convey the input or output. Resumption also requires protocol agreement on whether the client needs to replay prior input, or whether the server had already processed it.

issues.title: Bring back the end-to-end architecture diagram
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
The end-to-end architecture diagram from draft-zahed-agentproto-refarch was dropped. It showed users, agents, and tools over the agent
communication protocol, with its dialog, authorization and delegation, and identity management blocks, running over the transport and
security layers. The current figures show the network topology and the functional blocks separately, but not how ACP relates to transport and
security. Suggest bringing it back.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I brought back a simplified version of it into the section on interaction patterns.

issues.title: Multi-level identification
issues.author: khyao78
issues.body:
In the discussion yesterday, we tentatively agreed that a dialog refers to the conversation between two parties, while the dialog context is protocol-level metadata used to correlate multiple dialogs.

Then, regarding identification, do we need multi-level identifiers? Identifying both the dialog (dialog identifier) and the dialog context (dialog context identifier)?

The two identifiers serve different functions.

The dialog ID represents the independence of each dialog.

The dialog context ID is used for logical association/binding across multiple dialogs and can serve as the identifier for the complete envelope.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: We don't need two. I hope this is now clear in the document, there is a diagram on how delegation works.

issues.title: Participants in the dialog context meta-data
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
The Dialog Context definition lists “participants along with their identifiers and roles” as meta-data. Since ACP is two-party, the participants of a dialog are its two endpoints, and each learns the other’s identity by authenticating it at setup. An agent cannot list participants beyond its peer, since it does not know which agent downstream will eventually execute the task.

What does “participants” refer to, who populates it, and how does a receiver verify it? If it is the two endpoints, it is redundant with authentication and can be dropped from the meta-data.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I think this can be simplified to just the identity of the principal. THis does need to be stored as part of the meta-data. It needs to be remembered so that only that specific user can make further changes to the agentic dialog later on.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: Addressed most of this from a prior comment. Added in explciti mention of delegation chain identities as part of dialog context.

issues.title: Carrying a dialog across hops
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body:
Section 6.2.1 creates a new dialog for every delegation. A dialog also needs to continue across hops through relays, such as agent gateways and MCP proxies, and within a trust domain where local policy allows it.

Suggest: a new dialog is created at a trust boundary and wherever local policy requires it; otherwise a dialog can continue across hops.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: No, I fundamentally disagree with this. This is the same mistake with SIP proxies we made, introducing some kind of intermediary which isn't just a termination point. A relay or MCP proxy - those are all just going to be b2bua entities - terminating the dialog on one side and re-initiating on the other.

issues.title: Who creates the ADID
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: Section 6.1.1 does not say whether the client or the server generates the ADID. Suggest stating that the participant initiating the dialog generates it, so the receiver can verify the creator against the authenticated identity of the sender.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I disagree with this. The general rule of thumb is - the entity whcih owns the storage of the resource, needs to own generation of the identifier for the resource. In this case, it is the server which owns it, so the server needs to create it.

issues.title: Dialog context log
issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: The dialog context includes an append-only log of all inputs and outputs. Multi-device continuity works today with history kept by the server and fetched by the client, without the log being part of the protocol state. Suggest removing the log from the dialog context.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: But, dialog context *is* the state kept by the server and fetched by the client. So this comment seems inconsistent to me.

issues.author: tireddy2
issues.body: Section 8.4 describes one-to-many and many-to-many delivery among a dynamic group, which is outside the scope of the WG charter and conflicts with the two-party model in Section 5. You may want to remove it.

comments.author: zaheduzzaman
comments.body: Yes. I also have created a similar issue

issues.title: Session protocol ??
issues.author: zaheduzzaman
issues.body:
https://github.com/jdrosen/draft-manyfolks-agentproto-arch/blob/4c3a08c161718f9165dde87cf14c09083337470c/draft-manyfolks-agentproto-arch.md?plain=1#L108-L111

I would not mention session protocol here. During the BoF, it was clear that we are not talking about a session protocol as per say, rather a context management protocol. I also not think it is necessary to mention about SIP here.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I disagree exactly for the reason you are saying - this has come up many times. This document will be read and used standalone. It is introducing a new type of protocol that we've not had before in IETF, and that is going to require explanation. We should not assume that readers of this doc know the charter and remember the list discussion and so on.

comments.author: zaheduzzaman
comments.body:
But in the charter we are saying - ''The agentic dialog management protocol neither replaces application-layer agent communication protocols nor defines a new transport protocol."

and here in the text we are saying we need new session protocol. this to me contradicts. 

We the user/principals having dialog with the agent. I think we should then remove the sentence that we need a new session protocol, rather we need a new dialog management protocol.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: The entire first half of the doc - the text I contributed - goes to great lengths to try and just even define what a "dialog management protocol" is. It is "session-like" in that, we have to manage a lifecycle, we need to exchange data, we need to rehydrate and so on. This provides a useful frame of reference for comprehension, and I think that is important for this document. I do not read the charter as saying. "the word session must not appear in the document".

comments.author: zaheduzzaman
comments.body: I am fine with "session-like", lets be clear about it in the doc.

comments.author: jdrosen

issues.title: Where does the name come from?
issues.author: zaheduzzaman
issues.body:
https://github.com/jdrosen/draft-manyfolks-agentproto-arch/blob/4c3a08c161718f9165dde87cf14c09083337470c/draft-manyfolks-agentproto-arch.md?plain=1#L331

This is very close to DAWN  and discovery. It need to be described to avoid any confusion that discovery of the name is not within the scope here.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
Discovery is not in scope, but what this is saying is - the protocol needs to carry the name of the agent you are connceting too. Its basically going to be in the URI of the eventual protocol, e.g.:

POST example.com/agents/flight-booking

THe name of the agent is "flight-booking". 

If the protocol carried no naming whatsoever, we'd not be able to support basic multi-tenancy of a single IP or domain name supporting multiple agents, because we'd need to imply the agent being contacted from the IP. I don't think we should do that.

comments.author: zaheduzzaman
comments.body:
We have two cases -

1. "book me a flight to SF" - here the use does not provide any agent name, the required agent is discovered and used to fulfill the request. Hence the user to agent does not need to have a name of the agent. The discovery of the agent is out of scope.
2. "I want to connect to claude" - here we have a name of the agent, that need to be carried as part of conversation , where claude can be find is out of scope.
we need to be clear about it. Now it reads like we always have to know the name of the agent to initiate the session , which I think is not accurate assumption without describing how we are getting the name of the agents.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
Discovery is out of scope, no doubt about it.

I am thinking about cases where an enterprise hosts many agents. We should not assume that each enterprise (aka domain) has just one, and its like a super-agent which just loads skills based on what you ask.

Even if discovery is out of scope (which it is), this does not mean you cannot have an agent name in the protocol. Just like the web - every request to a web page includes its name (the HTTP URI). How you get that URI is out of scope of the HTTP protocol, but it doesnt mean HTTP can work without HTTP URIs. 

The thing I am talking about here is like the SIP URI or HTTP URI - the agent URI which identifies the agent.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: Revised the section on names, now titled, "Agents are IDentified by a URI". Also explicitly mention discovery is out of scope.

issues.title: Current document conflicts with charter
issues.author: zaheduzzaman
issues.body:
The charter says -

>> The dialog context consists of the identifiers and lifecycle state needed to correlate and maintain an agentic dialog. It does not include the content exchanged with AI models, such as conversation memory, retrieved documents, or prompts.

Now this conflicts with the whole concept of input, output, and feeding with the LLM context. At least the way it is written now. We need to fix this before publishing.

Also note that UI rendering related text are out of scope of the charter. We can perhaps rephrase them as exmaple usage.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body:
Firstly - charters are not meant to lock you into to terminology and data architectures that you cannot evolve as you build the protocol. 

Secondly - there is a fine distinction here, that we need more work to clarify. Clearly the protocol does care in some way about this content! It is exchanging it for sure. And, if we want to support things like recovery and rehydration, we also need to have this information stored as part of the protocol somewhere. To me, the distinction is that - ACP views these as typed blobs and doesn't care about what's inside, whereas the agent does. But I do think an implementation on the server would need to store it. And - looking forward to potential protocols - MOQT is a natural fit for the data exchange and nicely supports sync and recovery - and that would indeed count as storage. I also worry servers may need additional storage outside of the relay network, and I also don't want to mandate relays for the protocol to work.

So I think this bit requires a bit more discussion.

comments.author: jdrosen
comments.body: I made a few changes to address this, clarifying that LLM context is invisible to ACP; conversational continuity allows the agent to still decide how to map an agenic dialog to llm context and its outside the scope of ACP. I also added a section to clarify that log content is opaque to ACP, ACP cares only about meta-data.
